Added abs (Upper Rectus Abdominis, LowerRectus Abdominis) as secondary. The anterior load of the cable goblet squat places significant isometric demand on the core/rectus abdominis to prevent forward lean — confirmed by biomechanics sources. All other entries unchanged.

No changes. Primary Hamstrings (Biceps Femoris + Semitendinosus) correct. Secondary: glutes (hip stabilizer), Calves (gastrocnemius crosses the knee joint and assists knee flexion per EMG data), abs (standing unilateral requires isometric core stabilization). All confirmed.

Moved Gluteus Medius from primary to secondary. The Gluteus Maximus is the prime mover for hip extension in kickbacks; Gluteus Medius acts as a hip stabilizer/abductor (secondary role), not a primary hip extensor. Added oblique (External Obliques + Internal Obliques) as secondary — this is a unilateral standing exercise requiring anti-rotation core stabilization, per the rules for unilateral movements.
